description: AstraFlare is a multidisciplinary team brought together by a shared interest in solving meaningful challenges through research, technology, design and collaboration. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we are taking on a challenge that demands both scientific thinking and creative problem solving. Our team works by questioning assumptions, combining different strengths, and refining ideas until they become clear, useful and impactful. We value curiosity, teamwork and the courage to explore difficult problems in new ways.
summary: FireLens is a web-based fire intelligence platform developed by Team AstraFlare using NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS hotspot data to build a more consistent long-term fire history. It lets users choose an area and time period, explore a Burning Calendar, compare current fire activity with past patterns, see whether conditions are Normal, Elevated or Extreme, identify recurring and emerging fire zones, view a Priority Watchlist, understand why an area was flagged and download hotspot locations and monthly fire counts as CSV files. FireLens also includes Hotspot Heroes, a simple educational game that helps kids learn about wildfires and satellite data. By turning years of NASA fire observations into clear and useful insights, FireLens can help researchers, monitoring teams and communities understand unusual fire activity earlier, improve awareness and support smarter planning and safer decisions. The project aligns with SDG 13 – Climate Action, SDG 15 – Life on Land, SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities and SDG 4 – Quality Education.

How FireLens Addresses the Challenge

FireLens begins by harmonizing NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS active fire hotspot data. Because the two instruments observe fires differently, FireLens brings their records into a more consistent long-term fire history so users can study patterns across many years without focusing on the sensor differences.

CSV Data Export

FireLens also allows users to download CSV files containing hotspot locations and monthly fire counts for the selected area and date range.

This makes the data useful for researchers, analysts, and other users who want to perform further analysis.

Date Range Selection

Users can choose a specific area of interest and a date range to explore fire activity for the place and period they care about. The Burning Calendar then shows hotspot activity across months and years, making seasonal patterns, active periods and changes over time easier to understand.

Fire Fingerprint

The Fire Fingerprint gives a visual summary of the seasonal fire behavior of a region, while the Time Machine lets users move through different years and see how fire activity has changed over time.

Priority Watchlist

The platform identifies recurring fire zones, where fire activity appears repeatedly over time, and emerging fire zones, where fire activity has recently started increasing. A Priority Watchlist then helps users quickly see which areas may need closer monitoring.

Historical Comparison

FireLens also provides a historical comparison, where current fire activity is compared with past activity for the same period. From this, the platform performs anomaly detection and shows whether the current situation is Normal, Elevated or Extreme.

Hotspot Heroes: Educational Game

The game turns wildfire and satellite science into short, interactive missions so users can learn while playing.

Players first learn how to spot fire hotspots on a map. Then they explore the difference between MODIS and VIIRS and understand why the two fire records need to be harmonized. In another mission, players compare current fire activity with historical patterns and decide whether it is Normal, Elevated or Extreme.

MISSION

The game also teaches the difference between recurring fire zones, where fires appear repeatedly over time, and emerging fire zones, where fire activity has recently started increasing. In the final mission, players act as a Fire Response Commander and choose which area should receive monitoring attention first.

SCORE

After each mission, players receive points, simple explanations, and badges. This makes FireLens not only a monitoring and analysis platform, but also an engaging way to teach younger users about wildfire, NASA satellite data and fire awareness.

Project Impact

FireLens turns long term NASA fire data into clear and useful insights that help researchers, monitoring teams, land managers and communities understand unusual fire activity more quickly. By supporting earlier awareness, smarter monitoring, better planning and fire education, FireLens can contribute to safer and better informed communities.
